subject: Re: Post-call: Long-context evals — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Long-context evals — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Hi Samir — great to chat this morning. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of customer needs we heard today:
- Ingest and summarize long multi-document customer service threads (10–50k tokens) with high fidelity — minimal hallucination and strong extraction of entities and action items.
- Concern about truncation of the prompt and loss of context for later-turn summarization.
- Need a reproducible long-context eval run and clear quality baselines (ROUGE/ROUGE-L, faithfulness checks, entity extraction F1).
- Data residency in US and ability to run private evals on a Dedicated pool are important for procurement.

Model & eval recommendations (1st pass):
- Baselines: Llama-2-13B-chat (fp16) and Llama-2-70B-chat (fp16) for head-to-head.
- Production candidates: Redwood-optimized 13B-quant (int4) and 34B-quant (int8) — cost-friendly with good long-context memory in our prior tests.
- For very long sequences, run a sliding-window + KV-cache layout and compare to whole-context chunking to measure truncation artifacts.

Planned deliverables from Redwood:
1) Baseline eval run against your sample corpus using the prompt set attached (long_context_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt).
2) Benchmark CSV with per-model ROUGE/F1/hallucination-flag rates and qualitative examples (we'll include the worst 20 failures).
3) Doc describing recommended inference configs: batch sizes, KV cache strategy, quantization profile, and expected latency & cost estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Next steps / timeline:
- We will run the baseline on a sample of ~200 threads you shared (assume sanitized). Target to deliver results in 3 business days (EOD Mon, Aug 16).
- Schedule a 45-min follow-up on Tue Aug 17 to review results and pick model/pricing path.
- Procurement: Aditya will share a draft mutual action plan and initial pricing for Dedicated runs if you want to pursue private evaluation.

Attachments referenced: long_context_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompts + eval instructions), benchmark_summary_20260812.pdf (high-level approach).

Let me know if any of the recommended baselines are off or if you want us to prioritize a different model family.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Long-context evals — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before you run the baseline: 

1) Data residency: the sample corpus contains customer PII so we need the eval to run in our US-only Dedicated pool (not hosted). Can your team confirm that and share the needed onboarding steps?

2) Metrics: we care most about summarization fidelity (we'll use human judgements) and entity extraction F1 for SLA triggers. Can you include a lightweight faithfulness classifier or hallucination tagging in the CSV so we can triage?

3) Prompts: I glanced at the prompt set — looks broadly useful. Two asks: a) can you include a prompt variant that explicitly asks for 'source citations' (message index + excerpt) and b) make sure the extract format is JSONL for easy ingestion into our pipeline.

4) Timeframe: Aug 16 works but if you can get a draft CSV earlier (Aug 15 morning) that would help our internal review.

If you can confirm data residency and the hallucination tagging, we'll greenlight the sample run.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of NLP Applications
Acme Retail

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Long-context evals — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Samir — quick note from our side:

1) Data residency: confirmed — we can run the eval on a Dedicated US pool with customer-managed networking. Dev, looping you to own the onboarding checklist (VM images, KMS keys, sanitized sample transfer).

2) Hallucination tagging: we have a lightweight pipeline that flags hallucinations based on source overlap + entailment score. We'll include a hallucination_flag column and provide up to 3 example failing cases for human review.

3) Format: we'll produce CSV + JSONL extracts for the entity extraction outputs and the annotated summaries (so you can plug into your QA).

4) Procurement / pricing: Deal ID RDW-ACME-2026-08 has an initial pilot quote for a 30-day Dedicated evaluation. I'll post the draft MAP in HubSpot and share the link here: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789.

Proposed meeting windows for the follow-up review: Tue Aug 17 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue Aug 17 13:00–14:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — Aditya
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Long-context evals — recommended models, prompt sets, next steps

Samir — thanks, all set on our side. Confirming the plan and next steps: 

- We will run the baseline on your Dedicated US pool. Dev will reach out with onboarding instructions and a short checklist by EOD today.
- Deliverables: CSV + JSONL (entity extracts), hallucination_flag column, qualitative failing examples, and a short PDF with config recommendations.

- Timeline: baseline run will start Thu Aug 13 and we’ll aim to deliver a first-pass CSV by Mon Aug 16 EOD; if we can surface preliminary numbers by Aug 15 AM we will.

- Meeting: Tue Aug 17 10:00–11:00 PT confirmed. Calendar invite incoming.

See attached: long_context_eval_baseline_results.csv (we'll replace with final after the full run). Also attaching benchmark_summary_20260812.pdf which documents our methodology.

Thanks again — looking forward to the review.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
